title: Dynamic Head Tiling and Model Quirk Detector for Latency Stability
author: Maya Chen
commits: a1f9c3b: initial dynamic head-tiler prototype and API
d4b6f2e: add model quirk detector and profile registry
f3e8b44: epochal KV consolidation and eviction heuristics
b2aa9d1: integrate tiler into continuous-batcher and add hysteresis
c09d7f4: unit tests and perf benchmarks + CI adjustments
e7f5a22: docs and examples for ops runbook
description:
Context and motivation: Continuous-batching and KV-cache pressure remain the largest sources of token latency variance for long-running sessions on mixed-model fleets. This PR introduces a complementary approach that (1) detects model-specific quirks at load time (head-count asymmetry, MQA/GQA indicators, token-size growth patterns) and (2) applies a dynamic head-tiling strategy plus epochal KV consolidation to reduce kernel churn and stabilize latency under continuous batching. The goal: reduce p95 generation latency variance across Llama/Mistral/Qwen families while preserving token throughput and not regressing short-sequence latencies.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a lightweight quirk detector (serving/runtime/quirk_detector/model_profiles.py) that runs once per pinned model version and emits a small hint bundle (head_stride_hint, kv_eviction_policy, preferred_kernel_shapes). Hints are persisted to model_hints.yaml and can be toggled via admin config.
- Implements a dynamic head tiler (serving/runtime/scheduler/dynamic_tiler.py) that selects per-request tiling layouts based on detected quirks and current batch composition. The tiler supports both GQA and MQA modes and prefers fused stride layouts for heads with stable attention footprints.
- Introduces epochal KV consolidation (serving/runtime/kv/kv_consolidator.py) which consolidates fragmented KV slabs at low-traffic epochs to reduce eviction churn during bursts. Consolidation is throttled by a hysteresis window integrated into the continuous-batcher to avoid interfering with latency SLOs.
- Integrates the tiler into the continuous batcher, adding hysteresis to avoid oscillation when batch composition fluctuates rapidly.
- Adds unit and integration tests plus a small CI perf harness (serving/runtime/benchmarks/ci_perf_tests.sh) that runs a 30-minute long-run microbenchmark for p50/p95/p99 across a tiled and untiled baseline.

Checklist: [x] quirk detector prototype [x] dynamic tiler core [x] KV consolidator [x] tests + CI perf run [x] docs/ops runbook [x] backwards-compatible config toggles

Related work: builds on prior kernel-routing and KV-prefetch PRs (see ENG-3183, ENG-3372). This is intentionally conservative: all hints can be disabled per-model and the tiler falls back to the previous per-head default layout if metrics degrade.

Changed areas (high level):
- scheduler: new tiler module and tiler->batcher integration points (small surface changes in continuous-batcher)
- kv: consolidator module and minor eviction policy param additions
- configs: model hints registry and ops docs
- tests: deterministic microbench harness and unit tests for the detector/tiler

Review conversation (high level):
- Jonah Rivera (reviewer): "This looks promising, the tiler code is clear, but I saw a small perf regression on short 8-token sequences in the initial run. Can we add a guard so the tiler is a no-op below a configurable token threshold?"
  - Maya: "Added a token-length guard (default 32 tokens) and a config flag so ops can tune. See dynamic_tiler.py:tiler_select() for the check. Ran CI perf harness again and short-seq regression is gone."
- Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Quirk detector is neat — a couple nits: rename head_stride_hint -> head_layout_hint; add a tiny docstring on how MQA vs GQA influence the hint."
  - Maya: "Renamed and expanded docstring; updated docs/ops/quirk-detection.md with examples from Llama-2 and Mistral-7B"
- Evan Li (perf reviewer): "Please ensure consolidation doesn't cause a CPU spike on control-plane threads when many models consolidate at once."
  - Maya: "Added a concurrency rate limiter and randomized consolidation windows; added a test that simulates 200 model profiles consolidating concurrently."

CI and validation:
- First CI run: one flaky integration test failed (test_streaming_consumer) — root cause unrelated to tiling (external socket flakiness).
- Rerun: all checks passed. Perf harness results (stable run): p95 improvement averaged 12% on mixed MQA/GQA workloads; p99 improved by 5% on high token-length tails for Llama-2 and Qwen-2; no regression on 8–16 token microbenchmarks. Full result logs attached to CI artifact and linked in the Linear card.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior is off for models that do not have a hint bundle; new hints are opt-in via model pinning. Ops can enable hints globally via feature flags for canary namespaces.
- Rolling rollout plan: canary on non-critical production namespaces for 48h, observe p95/p99, expand if stable. If any regression >5% on p95 is observed, automatic rollback is triggered by the existing runtime rollout controller.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Jonah and Priya and green CI. Changelog entry added under Unreleased -> Performance: "Dynamic head tiling + model quirk detector: reduces p95 variance for mixed-model continuous-batching workloads (LLama/Mistral/Qwen)."
release_notes: Performance: Dynamic head tiling and model quirk detector to improve latency stability for mixed-model continuous-batching (opt-in via model_hints). Rollout: canary -> 48h -> expand, automatic rollback on p95 regressions.
